subject: Climate & Environment
title: Species Lost to Habitat Destruction
description: A short lesson to help you apply Species Lost to Habitat Destruction.

hook.text: Habitat destruction is the number one cause of species extinction worldwide.

buildup.text: Forests shelter over 80% of terrestrial species — from insects to great apes.

discovery.text: When a forest patch becomes too small, species that need large ranges vanish first.

twist.text: Fragmented forests create islands of habitat surrounded by farmland — trapping populations.

climax.text: Scientists estimate we lose dozens of species per day, most never documented.

punchline.text: We are erasing chapters of life before reading them.

quiz.question: What is the leading cause of species extinction?

details.summary: Tropical deforestation is the leading cause of species extinction, eliminating habitat for millions of organisms often before they are even discovered. An estimated 137 species go extinct every day due to rainforest destruction alone according to some models.
details.whyItMatters: Each species lost is a permanent diminishment of Earth's biological heritage. Forests hold most terrestrial biodiversity, making deforestation an extinction engine.
takeaways: Tropical forests hold over half of all terrestrial species
Many species have tiny ranges and disappear when their patch is cleared
Extinction from habitat loss is usually permanent and irreversible

faq.question: How many species go extinct from deforestation?
faq.answer: Exact numbers are uncertain because most tropical species are undescribed. Conservative models estimate thousands of extinctions per year from tropical deforestation alone, with many species vanishing before science ever knew they existed.

faq.question: Why are endemic species at the greatest risk?
faq.answer: Endemic species exist in only one location. When their specific habitat patch is cleared, there is no backup population elsewhere. Many tropical endemics have ranges measured in just a few square kilometers.
